name: A change to how a game plays updates its README in the same change
instruction: When a diff changes a game's controls, round length (shots, time or lives), point values, or how a round ends in `game.ts`, the same diff MUST update that game's `README.md` so that its How to play and Scoring sections match the new code. A change to a constant or value that the README states counts as such a change, even when the diff shows only the constant: water cannon's `TANK_SIZE` is its number of shots, and its target speeds set its points. Every number the README states must match the code. A README that describes an option or control the code no longer has fails.
relevant_when: The diff changes a game's game.ts in a way a player would notice, including a change to a constant for shots, time, lives, speeds or points that the game's README states. Return not applicable for refactors, renames, drawing-only changes and test-only changes.
context: PR #28 had to remove a `?shots=` option that the water cannon README described but the code didn't have. Doc gardening catches this kind of drift later; this check catches it in the pull request that causes it. House rule 6 in AGENTS.md. A diff that changes only README.md is out of scope: a diff verifier sees only the changed files, so the judge would have no game.ts to compare with. The doc gardening loop checks every game's README against its code.
scope_reason: The rule is about game.ts and README.md changing together, which only the diff shows.

checklist.name: readme-updated-with-behaviour
checklist.rule: A diff that changes controls, round length, point values or how a round ends in a game's game.ts, including through a constant such as TANK_SIZE, also changes that game's README.md.

checklist.name: readme-numbers-match-code
checklist.rule: Every control, count and point value the changed README states matches the code in game.ts, and the README names no option or control the code doesn't have.

references.note: House rule 6: each game has a README that stays true to the code.
